column1: # Consolidate the prior listener and framed-command seams into the first real TCP connection owner.

column9: The prior bounded framed dispatch and incremental result authority are retained and now execute over one real TcpStream lifecycle with explicit authentication, unsupported-command ERR responses, peer-close isolation, and exactly-once connection accounting; TLS, compression negotiation on this socket, prepared statements, public authentication, and concurrency remain open.

The existing bind and listener lifecycle is retained while the serial node becomes the first owner that accepts and completely serves a real MySQL connection; Unix sockets, PROXY protocol, status HTTP, graceful process shutdown, and concurrent admission remain open.
